signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.51, holding above its SMA20 at 156.40 while remaining below the SMA50/200 cluster around 158.45/158.60. An overnight OIS differential of SOFR 3.88% vs TONA 0.98% secures a +290bp carry advantage for the dollar, anchoring spot demand while VIX at 14.9 confirms a low-volatility environment where carry strategies typically dominate. However, options pricing exhibits strong structural caution, with 25d risk reversals marked at -2.28 put skew and 1M ATM implied volatility at 8.7% vs 30-day realized volatility of 10.1%, generating a -1.5% volatility risk premium. Furthermore, the MOVE index sits at the 96th percentile of its trailing year while VIX sits at the 8th, highlighting bond market volatility pricing central bank path uncertainty that equities are not reflecting. Leveraged Funds pared JPY longs by -15,597 contracts WoW to leave net positioning at +4,472, though 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention warnings. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-driven upside constrained by options downside skew. Catalyst: Fed Governor Bowman speech at 12:15 UTC. Risk: US 10Y yields drop sharply below 5.00%, compressing the US-Japan rate gap and triggering rapid carry liquidation.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme vs Spec Short
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5652, suppressed firmly beneath its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster between 0.5789 and 0.5853. Leveraged Funds hold net short positions of -5,216 contracts following a weekly reduction of -2,897 contracts, whereas retail positioning on Retail sentiment data displays an extreme 92% net-long exposure. This acute retail-versus-institutional positioning divergence develops as Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75% provides a +125bp carry premium supporting the dollar, compounded by the 2Y NZ-US sovereign spread widening 27bp in the dollar's favor over the past 20 sessions to -88bp. Retail dip-buyers are fighting persistent structural macro divergence and lower moving-average resistance. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, retail capitulation setup against institutional trend. Catalyst: United States JOLTS Job Openings at 14:00 UTC. Risk: US labor data softens significantly, driving a broad dollar pullback above the 0.5700 handle.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Technical Compression + Real Yield Shift
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1379, remaining below its SMA20 at 1.1539, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1625. Leveraged Funds maintain an extended net short position of -58,805 contracts (37.3% long share) after selling an additional -7,450 contracts WoW. The policy backdrop reinforces this downward momentum, as Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% establishes a +135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, with Germany-US 2Y spreads widening -20bp toward the greenback over the trailing 20 sessions to -158bp. Cross-asset dynamics highlight this decoupling, with EUR/USD correlation to the EuroStoxx breaking to -0.009 against a 252-day norm of +0.145 (z = -1.60σ). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, moving-average resistance capping upside. Catalyst: Euro Area Economic Sentiment Indicator and Consumer Price Expectations at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Eurozone inflation expectations print sharply above forecast, accelerating ECB rate hike pricing.
